### Prerequisites (listed separately)

1. LATE -> ERR, form state. `policy_source` "The fulfillment fee refund is not worked out until every return authorization on the order that has been received back for a Tailwise error carries its refund entry." — verbatim in `late_delivery_fee_refund_acda101e` (LATE hub, Basis para 2); in no other document (script check). Connective "not ... until" preserved. Resolution: the sentence's words "received back", "Tailwise error", "refund entry" reach `tailwise_error_return_refund_8249b015` ("When an item has come back ... in status received", "each a Tailwise error", "Once booked, the order history carries a return refund entry for that line and authorization"); record: RMA 5204560a status received, reason not_as_described. Strength: hard gate in source and KB. Value effect carried by `error_settled_fee_share_b7e318bb` (source `error_settled` ladder).
2. LATE -> DMG, form state. `policy_source` "Before the fulfillment fee refund is worked out, every damage report on the order that was declined because the damaged item stays with the customer must carry its returnless damage credit wherever the customer takes the money back rather than a replacement." — verbatim in the LATE hub (Basis para 3); in no other document. Connective "Before ... must" and the condition "wherever the customer takes the money back" preserved. Resolution: "damage report ... declined because the damaged item stays with the customer" is defined in the same words in `returnless_damage_credit_72cad481` para 1, which describes the write ("Once booked, the order history carries a damage credit entry for that line"); record: RMA ea58d33a reason damaged, status rejected. Strength equal.
- Neither ERR nor DMG documents carry either sentence or mention the late-delivery fee refund (script scan: no "late-delivery" / "fulfillment fee refund" in any ERR or DMG document). `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect` have no home in any document.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** No KB-BIJECTION defect in the LATE/ERR/DMG domain, its base refs or the retired surface.

Policy-side notes (nature recorded; verdict unchanged; untriggered in this task):
1. Retained parameters of retired clauses. The source retires "The fulfillment fee is refunded only when every line is returned for a Tailwise error and shipping_refund_on_error_return is true" and the base refund basis (`refund_price_basis`), yet keeps both parameters in the variants with schema meanings phrased as rules ("whether the fulfillment fee is refunded when every line is returned for a Tailwise error"; "amount refunded for a returned unit"). The KB renders the parameters faithfully in `return_methods_deductions_982b7463` ("Fulfillment fee refunded when every line is returned for a Tailwise error | Yes ..."; "Amount refunded for a returned unit | Price paid after allocated discounts") beside `return_rules_557ad3ba` 3.1/3.3 marked retired, so the corpus shows the same tension the source has. This is a source-layer inconsistency (parameter outliving its clause), not a KB legislating or dropping anything.
2. Coverage gap after the ERR overwrite: the ERR rule sends non-error returns to "the base return rule", but the base refund-basis clause is retired by ERR's own overwrite; the in-force base text keeps only the deductions clause for changed-mind returns. Carried faithfully ("refunded under the general return rules"); source-side.
3. ERR and DMG baselines themselves enumerate their credits by name ("plus the error allowance, the refund-wait credit ..."), so the computation documents' enumeration is the source's form.
4. Factor nesting in the source: `basket_valuation` decides the basket value that `basket_value` reads; the KB carries it in the source's words.
